title: How do I train a general AI on a board game where the board can be a variable directed graph?
author: FortunaWolf
selftext:
Hi! I hope this is an appropriate place for my question. 

I am making a board game and want to train some AI to play it (for providing opponents in solo play on the computer and to make agents who can develop and learn strategies faster than human play testers so I can optimize the game parameters). 

The game board will usually consist of 2 to 100 stars, which of which are connected to neighbors and some connections may be directed or have other special conditions attached. Its possible that I may allow connections to change during gameplay. 

In the board game training lessons and tutorials the boards are always static, so you can feed the AI the states of every position on the board and it will naturally learn how the board is connected, but that is not the case here and I don't want to have to train an AI for every possible game board.

Is this a solved problem and how do people deal with it?

Thanks!

comments.author: AbstractBG
comments.body: I've trained AI for board games using an AlphaZero based approach, so that is one avenue. However, a full AlphaZero implementation is time consuming and computationally expensive, so I recommend taking an approach like [https://github.com/harbecke/HexHex](https://github.com/harbecke/HexHex) to begin with.

replies.author: FortunaWolf
replies.body: Thanks, I am fine with trying the alpha zero approach, I just want to know what format I should feed the game state to it in, in particular, having a variable graph as a board. Or will an Alpha Zero approach just chew through most anything you throw at it?

replies.author: AbstractBG
replies.body: You have many options between CNNs, Transformers, GNNs, or MLPs. I recommend finding the simplest possible representations which captures the full state and using that. It sounds like you could embed a neighboring connectively information as a feature plane and then train a standard Resnet on top of that.
